dedupe_keys.name: areal statistics of urban tree canopy for the miami dade urban area 2020

description: This dataset summarises urban tree canopy across the developed area of Miami-Dade County, Florida, for 2020, on five sets of areal units: parcels, census block groups, census places, municipalities and county commission districts. It was produced by researchers at Florida International University led by Hartwig Hochmair and published in 2021 on the FIU Research Data Portal. For every polygon it gives four percentages: existing tree canopy, possible canopy on pervious surfaces such as grass and bare ground, possible canopy on impervious surfaces such as parking lots, and area unsuitable for canopy such as buildings, streets and railways. Coverage is the urban development area of Miami-Dade County. Access: a zipped Esri file geodatabase with five polygon feature classes, downloadable from the portal. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC0-1.0. Access is free of charge. Caveats: a single 2020 snapshot derived from land-cover classification, so small trees and recent changes may be missed. Simulation uses are urban heat mitigation and shade planning, prioritising tree planting in streets and public space, and heat exposure models at parcel scale. Related records: the 3-30-300 urban greening datasets and the London green roof survey.
